concepts.applicability: Scientific interpretation of resonant visualization demonstrations and studies.
concepts.limitations: A beautiful geometric figure does not establish the same frequency-to-shape mapping across media, or any health effect.
concepts.summary: Cymatics is a broad descriptive term for visible patterns produced by vibration or acoustically driven motion in plates, surfaces, fluids or particles. Different experiments involve different physical mechanisms; the name does not identify a single universal geometry-producing force.
concepts.title: Cymatics as visualized vibration

concepts.applicability: Small-amplitude linear-wave approximation.
concepts.limitations: In nonlinear media, superposition may fail and harmonics, mode coupling or instabilities may dominate.
concepts.summary: For linear wave equations the displacement from multiple solutions is their sum. Relative phase determines constructive and destructive interference; apparent stationary structure can be produced by counterpropagating components.
concepts.title: Wave superposition

concepts.applicability: Specify which field is measured: displacement, velocity or acoustic pressure.
concepts.limitations: A camera image of deposited grains is not a direct map of pressure; particle transport is an additional process.
concepts.summary: A node is a location of zero displacement for a standing displacement field; an antinode is a region of high displacement amplitude. A pressure node is not automatically the same location as a displacement node.
concepts.title: Nodes and antinodes

concepts.applicability: Small-signal linear model for discrete resonances.
concepts.limitations: Not every visible pattern is an undamped eigenmode, and a resonance peak depends on drive placement and losses.
concepts.summary: A structure has normal modes determined by its geometry, material properties and constraints. Near some modal frequencies a driven response can be amplified, with magnitude shaped by damping and forcing configuration.
concepts.title: Resonance and normal modes

concepts.applicability: Periodic steady-state measurements.
concepts.limitations: Do not confuse driving frequency with a structure’s eigenfrequency or a subharmonic response.
concepts.summary: Frequency f is cycles per second in hertz; period T=1/f for a periodic signal, and angular frequency omega=2*pi*f. A frequency alone does not encode field geometry.
concepts.title: Frequency, period and angular frequency

concepts.applicability: Each material and geometry requires its own wave model.
concepts.limitations: Faraday-wave forcing and dissipation can alter wavenumber selection beyond the free-wave approximation.
concepts.summary: A dispersion relation links angular frequency and wavenumber. Bending waves and gravity-capillary surface waves have different relations, so identical excitation frequencies do not imply identical wavelengths or patterns.
concepts.title: Dispersion

concepts.applicability: Boundary values must reflect physical mounting.
concepts.limitations: A centre-clamped demonstration plate is not equivalent to a plate supported on every edge.
concepts.summary: Fixed, free, clamped and simply supported boundaries impose different constraints on displacement, slope, bending moment or force; they change accessible normal modes.
concepts.title: Boundary conditions

concepts.applicability: Thickness much smaller than in-plane spans; small deflections; negligible transverse shear in the thin-plate regime.
concepts.limitations: Thick plates, anisotropy, pre-stress, fluid loading and nonlinear deflections need different models.
concepts.summary: Thin, uniform, homogeneous, isotropic plates can be represented by a linear bending equation relating flexural rigidity, areal mass and transverse displacement.
concepts.title: Kirchhoff–Love plate approximation

concepts.applicability: Uniform plate; exact simply supported boundary conditions.
concepts.limitations: This analytical expression is NOT a prediction for a centre-clamped free-edge Chladni plate.
concepts.summary: For a thin isotropic rectangle simply supported on all four edges, sinusoidal separable modes yield frequencies proportional to [(m/Lx)^2+(n/Ly)^2] times sqrt(D/(rho*h)).
concepts.title: Rectangular simply supported plate spectrum

concepts.applicability: Only exact for the idealized simply supported rectangle.
concepts.limitations: Grain accumulation requires dynamics not supplied by this eigenfunction alone.
concepts.summary: The modal displacement basis has the form sin(m*pi*x/Lx)*sin(n*pi*y/Ly) for positive integer m,n. Nodes occur where the amplitude vanishes; the entire boundary is nodal for this support condition.
concepts.title: Mode shapes on a simply supported rectangle

concepts.applicability: Keep material and support model fixed while varying thickness.
concepts.limitations: Thicker specimens may violate thin-plate assumptions or alter mounting.
concepts.summary: In the Kirchhoff–Love expression with fixed E, nu, rho and in-plane dimensions, the natural frequency scales linearly with plate thickness because D scales with h^3 while mass per area scales with h.
concepts.title: Thickness scaling invariant

concepts.applicability: Geometrically similar plate in-plane dimensions, fixed thickness.
concepts.limitations: Does not describe a full similarity transform that scales thickness too.
concepts.summary: Scaling both plate spans by s with fixed material, thickness and support yields f proportional to 1/s^2 in the ideal simply supported bending model.
concepts.title: In-plane geometric scaling invariant

concepts.applicability: Exact geometric and material symmetry.
concepts.limitations: A frequency-to-picture lookup need not be unique; tiny imperfections can split degenerate frequencies.
concepts.summary: In a square isotropic simply supported plate, modes indexed (m,n) and (n,m) share a natural frequency. Their linear combinations can have different nodal geometries at the same frequency.
concepts.title: Degenerate modes and pattern ambiguity

concepts.applicability: Approximately linear response with identifiable modes.
concepts.limitations: Peak widths depend on instrument response, forcing, overlaps and nonlinearities; a high-Q assumption may fail.
concepts.summary: Damping limits the amplitude of driven resonances and broadens response peaks; a quality factor or damping ratio can summarize the sharpness of a sufficiently isolated mode.
concepts.title: Damping and resonance width

concepts.applicability: Wood, composites and rolled sheets may be directionally stiff.
concepts.limitations: Do not fit an isotropic model and infer material identity without examining anisotropy.
concepts.summary: When stiffness varies by direction, mode shapes and frequencies differ from isotropic formulas, even at the same dimensions and mass density.
concepts.title: Orthotropic and anisotropic plates

concepts.applicability: Driven, linear regime with a specified excitation point and amplitude.
concepts.limitations: A weak or missing resonance in one setup is not proof the corresponding eigenmode is absent.
concepts.summary: Driving a plate near a nodal region of a particular mode can excite that mode weakly; the observed response is determined by the modal coupling of the forcing distribution.
concepts.title: Excitation position and modal observability

concepts.applicability: A suitable plate, low-mass particles, and sufficient drive.
concepts.limitations: Not a direct reconstruction of the underlying displacement phase or pressure field; grain size, friction and acceleration matter.
concepts.summary: Dispersed grains on a vibrating plate can migrate and settle near low-motion nodal regions, creating visible Chladni figures that vary with frequency and geometry.
concepts.title: Chladni plate method

concepts.applicability: Granular demonstration with particles on a solid surface.
concepts.limitations: A pure structural eigenmode solver does not calculate particle trajectories or final grain densities.
concepts.summary: The time-dependent grain pattern reflects repeated contact, sliding, impact, airflow, friction and vibration; the stabilized image depends on both plate dynamics and particle dynamics.
concepts.title: Granular transport mechanisms

concepts.applicability: History of acoustic demonstrations.
concepts.limitations: Different plates, supports and frequencies do not encode universal symbols independent of the apparatus.
concepts.summary: Chladni figures are named for the experiments that made vibrational modes visible with fine particles on plates. The historical method is a demonstration of mechanical modes, not evidence of a universal hidden geometric code.
concepts.title: Ernst Chladni and historical context

concepts.applicability: Controlled camera images with known plate geometry.
concepts.limitations: A compelling photograph without raw capture and a reference scale does not establish quantitative mode geometry.
concepts.summary: An image-based comparison should register the plate boundary, correct lens perspective, record illumination and provide segmentation uncertainty before extracting spatial signatures.
concepts.title: Image acquisition of nodal patterns

concepts.applicability: Fluid depth, viscosity, surface tension and drive amplitude are specified.
concepts.limitations: Surface wave behavior is not equivalent to Chladni plate bending; forcing and dissipation are central.
concepts.summary: When a fluid container is driven vertically at sufficient acceleration, the free surface may develop standing patterns through parametric instability; a subharmonic response is often encountered.
concepts.title: Faraday waves and parametric forcing

concepts.applicability: Driven surface-wave experiment.
concepts.limitations: A visible onset threshold must be measured and cannot be read from simple free-wave dispersion alone.
concepts.summary: A flat liquid surface can remain stable at low forcing and develop periodic waves after an instability threshold depending on depth, viscosity, frequency and surface tension.
concepts.title: Instability threshold

concepts.applicability: Linear surface gravity-capillary waves when forcing and viscosity are negligible.
concepts.limitations: Do not substitute a free-wave expression as a full Faraday-wave model.
concepts.summary: Surface waves are shaped by both gravity and surface tension, with wavenumber and finite depth affecting frequency; viscous and parametrically driven cases need extended treatments.
concepts.title: Gravity-capillary dispersion

concepts.applicability: Driven fluids near pattern formation thresholds.
concepts.limitations: Avoid treating every visible multi-fold surface shape as a linear eigenmode.
concepts.summary: Near or beyond parametric onset, multiple surface modes can interact and compete. Bifurcations may be supercritical or subcritical depending on physical parameters.
concepts.title: Nonlinear mode competition

concepts.applicability: Linear small-amplitude acoustics.
concepts.limitations: Sound pressure measurement in air does not directly reveal a plate’s displacement field.
concepts.summary: In gases and liquids, sound fields are often characterized by time-varying pressure and particle velocity. Standing pressure fields are distinct from plate displacement modes and require fluid acoustics modeling.
concepts.title: Acoustic pressure field

concepts.applicability: Small particles and acoustic field regimes specified by a suitable force model.
concepts.limitations: Particles do not always move toward pressure nodes; acoustic contrast and other forces matter.
concepts.summary: Time-averaged momentum transfer from an acoustic wave can exert forces on particles; its direction and strength depend on particle properties, fluid and wave geometry.
concepts.title: Acoustic radiation force

concepts.applicability: Viscous-fluid acoustics.
concepts.limitations: Do not interpret all particle trajectories as radiation-force phenomena.
concepts.summary: Absorption and boundary layers can generate steady or slowly varying fluid flows in an oscillating acoustic field; these flows can transport particles independently of radiation forces.
concepts.title: Acoustic streaming

concepts.applicability: Coupled structural-fluid system.
concepts.limitations: Uncoupled vacuum-plate eigenfrequencies are not necessarily valid when immersed in water.
concepts.summary: A vibrating structure can drive an adjacent fluid and the fluid can load and shift the structure’s response, especially in immersed or thin structures.
concepts.title: Fluid-structure coupling

concepts.applicability: Suitable object size, acoustic contrast, power and geometry.
concepts.limitations: Levitation evidence does not imply unrestricted manipulation of arbitrary objects or medical efficacy.
concepts.summary: Structured acoustic pressure fields can stably position some small objects using radiation forces; phased arrays and holographic fields enable advanced field control.
concepts.title: Acoustic levitation and trapping

concepts.applicability: Coherent acoustic drive and correctly designed holographic element.
concepts.limitations: An acoustic hologram is a phase-engineering method, not a spontaneous Chladni code.
concepts.summary: A spatially patterned transmission or reflection element can shape ultrasonic phase and amplitude, producing designed acoustic fields for experimental manipulation.
concepts.title: Acoustic holograms

concepts.applicability: Scientific observation intended for later reanalysis.
concepts.limitations: A derived spectrum or image alone may omit calibration and procedural confounders.
concepts.summary: A reproducible run should preserve original waveform, camera frames, sensor traces, equipment settings, timestamps, sample geometry, units and raw-file hashes.
concepts.title: Raw data and provenance

concepts.applicability: Well-defined measurands and calibrated instruments.
concepts.limitations: A label such as "calibrated" without a certificate, date, range or uncertainty is not sufficient.
concepts.summary: Instrument calibration links a measured quantity to reference standards and a stated uncertainty through an unbroken documented chain, where applicable.
concepts.title: Calibration and traceability

concepts.applicability: Measured frequency, length, thickness, acceleration, temperature, etc.
concepts.limitations: Uncertainty is not the same as an error or a confidence score assigned by an agent.
concepts.summary: A measurement result is incomplete for quantitative comparison without a statement of uncertainty appropriate to its method; both repeatability and systematic components may matter.
concepts.title: Measurement uncertainty

concepts.applicability: Predeclared measurement protocol and comparisons.
concepts.limitations: Re-running a deterministic formula does not validate its physical model.
concepts.summary: Repeatability holds conditions nearly constant; reproducibility deliberately changes conditions such as operator, equipment, batch or lab. Both help identify sensitivity and robustness.
concepts.title: Repeatability and reproducibility

concepts.applicability: Supervised evaluation with access to held-out ground truth.
concepts.limitations: Training and evaluating on the same nominal patterns exaggerates generalization.
concepts.summary: To test pattern identification fairly, register expected labels and scoring methods, hide the test condition from the classifier, then evaluate held-out plates or repeats.
concepts.title: Blinded mode identification

concepts.applicability: Controlled experiments with documented apparatus and safety procedure.
concepts.limitations: Ultrasonic systems and high-amplitude mechanical shakers require hardware-specific precautions; this atlas is not a safety certification.
concepts.summary: Record acoustic power, voltage, peak acceleration, mounting pressure, temperature, fluid properties and exposure conditions, because these can change observed patterns.
concepts.title: Drive level, environmental conditions and safety

concepts.applicability: Digitized time signals with known sampling chain.
concepts.limitations: A peak below Nyquist can still be an alias when higher-frequency content is present.
concepts.summary: Uniform sampling at rate Fs can only represent certain bandlimited signal content without aliasing. Anti-alias filtering and sufficient bandwidth are essential when estimating frequencies.
concepts.title: Sampling rate and aliasing

concepts.applicability: Finite-time Fourier spectral estimates.
concepts.limitations: Peak magnitude depends on window normalization and bin alignment; do not compare arbitrary FFT plots without metadata.
concepts.summary: A finite observation interval can spread sinusoidal energy across spectral bins; windows trade resolution, leakage behavior and amplitude calibration.
concepts.title: Spectral leakage and window functions

concepts.applicability: Linear or specified nonlinear experiment.
concepts.limitations: A spectrogram of a sweep is not by itself a mode-shape measurement; drive drift confounds peak comparisons.
concepts.summary: A controlled frequency sweep records response versus drive frequency and can reveal resonance peaks. Each sample should include actual input amplitude and timing.
concepts.title: Frequency response sweep

concepts.applicability: Testable research design rather than a proven unique fingerprint.
concepts.limitations: Isospectral or nearly degenerate cases and uncertain supports can defeat unique identification.
concepts.summary: A useful resonance signature may combine a calibrated spectrum with registered displacement maps, instrument context, modal uncertainty and provenance, rather than a bare frequency list.
concepts.title: Spectral-spatial resonance signature

concepts.applicability: Images or laser-scanned mode maps after coordinate registration.
concepts.limitations: Visual similarity need not imply matching material or boundary conditions.
concepts.summary: Useful spatial descriptors can include connected nodal regions, symmetry class, registered spatial frequencies and mode-shape correlations. Their robustness should be measured under image noise and alignment errors.
concepts.title: Nodal-pattern feature extraction

concepts.applicability: Inverse estimation from limited measurements.
concepts.limitations: A single observed Chladni pattern or tone cannot reliably reveal arbitrary material composition.
concepts.summary: Different combinations of geometry, material, thickness, supports and loading may produce similar or overlapping spectral information, creating non-identifiability.
concepts.title: Inverse identification is often non-unique

concepts.applicability: Bayesian or constrained inverse inference.
concepts.limitations: A model fit without out-of-sample evidence or residual checks is not a scientific identification.
concepts.summary: Specify plausible material, plate thickness, geometry and boundary conditions before fitting; compare alternative model families rather than forcing a single favorite explanation.
concepts.title: Prior constraints and model selection

concepts.applicability: Matched observations and forward predictions.
concepts.limitations: Small residuals alone do not prove the assumed physical model is unique or correctly calibrated.
concepts.summary: Compare predicted and observed frequencies and mode shapes with error bars, recording discrepancies and systematic trends. Residual structure can reveal wrong support or material assumptions.
concepts.title: Residual and uncertainty diagnostics

concepts.applicability: Specific device geometry, particle contrasts and controlled biocompatibility.
concepts.limitations: These methods are application-dependent and do not demonstrate universal frequency-specific biological effects.
concepts.summary: Acoustofluidic devices exploit ultrasound-induced forces and flows to align or transport selected particles and cells in microfluidic channels.
concepts.title: Particle and cell sorting by acoustics

concepts.applicability: Engineered in-vitro experimental systems.
concepts.limitations: Application research is not a claim that audible music cures disease or recodes DNA.
concepts.summary: Peer-reviewed studies investigate acoustic assembly and spatial organization of particles, cells and biofabrication materials using standing waves.
concepts.title: Patterned biological assembly

concepts.applicability: Instrumented structure with comparable baseline configurations.
concepts.limitations: Detecting a modal shift is not automatically a unique diagnosis of the root cause.
concepts.summary: Modal measurements can reveal changes in stiffness, damping or constraints and support engineering condition-monitoring hypotheses when calibrated against reference data.
concepts.title: Vibration-based structural diagnostics

concepts.applicability: Laboratory transducers with specified wavelength, phase control and operating environment.
concepts.limitations: These techniques should not be conflated with ordinary visible Chladni figures.
concepts.summary: Acoustic holograms and phased ultrasound can produce selected spatial pressure patterns for manipulation, levitation and laboratory instrumentation.
concepts.title: Designed acoustic field manipulation

concepts.applicability: All knowledge services and agent retrieval tasks.
concepts.limitations: Document hashes detect changes but do not establish that a claim is true.
concepts.summary: A linked reference summary, mathematical derivation, synthetic computation and physical measurement have different evidentiary standing. Agent-generated summaries must remain candidates until reviewed.
concepts.title: Evidence levels must remain distinct

concepts.applicability: Local research amortization workflows.
concepts.limitations: A packet is not an unrestricted answer, and an admitted packet can still later be revised or retracted.
concepts.summary: A source-linked research packet can preserve a bounded claim, assumptions, scope, timestamp, rights, provenance and review decision so multiple systems reuse the same qualified evidence.
concepts.title: Evidence packets as reusable atomic units

concepts.applicability: Repositories integrating time-sensitive publications.
concepts.limitations: A retrieval hit or recently generated answer does not refresh a source itself.
concepts.summary: Reference metadata should track checked versions, retractions, conflicts, and freshness. Unknown or stale evidence should be disclosed and routed to fresh research instead of cited as current fact.
concepts.title: Refresh and invalidation

concepts.applicability: Connected local models, agents and tools.
concepts.limitations: Serialization alone does not guarantee the receiving model applies source limitations correctly.
concepts.summary: Versioned machine-readable records and read-only retrieval routes let independent agents request the same scoped scientific context with stable identifiers and explicit citations.
concepts.title: Cross-system transport contracts

concepts.applicability: Scientific interpretation of cymatics demonstrations.
concepts.limitations: Absence of a universal law does not diminish valid applications of resonant patterning.
concepts.summary: Identical frequencies do not necessarily create the same pattern across materials and boundaries. Unsupported claims about universal number codes, disease cures or specific material transformations should be left unverified.
concepts.title: Avoiding universal-frequency claims

concepts.applicability: For vertically oscillated liquid layers within the assumptions of the model; quantitative thresholds depend on viscosity, depth, geometry and forcing.
concepts.limitations: The classical ideal-fluid stability model cannot be treated as a calibrated prediction for an arbitrary real fluid or container.
concepts.summary: Parametric excitation of a liquid surface can be analyzed through stability of periodically forced modes; instability regions depend on forcing amplitude and frequency. This is a threshold phenomenon rather than a one-frequency one-pattern rule.
concepts.title: Mathieu-type parametrically driven free-surface instability

concepts.applicability: Ultrasonic particle manipulation with particle radius and boundary-layer thickness both small compared with wavelength.
concepts.limitations: Not a general solution for arbitrary particles, elastic shapes, wavelengths or turbulence.
concepts.summary: Radiation-force models for small compressible spheres in viscous fluids include a viscous boundary layer and can differ from ideal-fluid approximations.
concepts.title: Viscous corrections to acoustic radiation force

concepts.applicability: Small spheres relative to wavelength; thermoviscous fluid and appropriately described particle material.
concepts.limitations: The cited paper provides conditional theoretical predictions; a reversal is not guaranteed for all experiments.
concepts.summary: Thermoviscous theory predicts that dissipative fluid and particle properties can alter the direction and magnitude of the acoustic radiation force, including size-dependent sign changes in some material systems.
concepts.title: Thermoviscous size-dependent particle contrast

concepts.applicability: Ideal-fluid, long-wavelength, small-particle regime; analyze departures from these assumptions separately.
concepts.limitations: A bibliographic record establishes the historical work, not the range of agreement with a particular viscous experiment.
concepts.summary: Gor'kov's classic treatment concerns forces on small particles in ideal acoustic fluids and motivates later radiation-force approximations.
concepts.title: Gor'kov ideal-fluid small-particle force model

concepts.applicability: Spatial wavefront design using the acoustic medium, source and fabricated hologram configuration of the research.
concepts.limitations: Not every Chladni pattern is an acoustic hologram; field reconstruction efficiency and resolution depend on device conditions.
concepts.summary: A fabricated holographic phase profile can reconstruct a complex acoustic field when illuminated by an appropriate coherent source. Acoustic holograms have been demonstrated for contact-free field shaping.
concepts.title: Phase-encoded acoustic hologram reconstruction

concepts.applicability: Measurements with a defined procedure, repeatability statistics, instrument calibration and traceability where applicable.
concepts.limitations: Uncertainty is not the same as error or experimental proof; a poorly specified measurand cannot be repaired by extra decimal places.
concepts.summary: NIST TN 1297 provides guidance for evaluating and expressing measurement uncertainty. Report the measurand, units, identified uncertainty contributors and the method used to combine them.
concepts.title: Measurement uncertainty and stated error budget

concepts.applicability: Scientific reporting in SI or clearly documented conversion units.
concepts.limitations: The existence of a current brochure does not validate calibration or measurements in an individual experiment.
concepts.summary: The BIPM SI Brochure ninth edition has a revised version published in June 2026; unit definitions and presentation should cite the appropriate dated revision.
concepts.title: SI standard: latest revision and unit conventions

concepts.applicability: Machine-readable research lineage, transform metadata, author/reviewer attributions and versioned exports.
concepts.limitations: A provenance graph proves only recorded relationships when authenticated; it does not certify scientific correctness or the actor's true identity.
concepts.summary: W3C PROV-O defines interoperable vocabulary for representing entities, activities, agents and relations between the artifacts and processes of research.
concepts.title: Provenance graph: entities, activities and agents

concepts.applicability: Science-literature synthesis consumed by agents without automatic source access.
concepts.limitations: Verifying a source abstract is not equivalent to reading full methods or independently confirming an empirical result.
concepts.summary: A bibliographic catalog entry, publisher abstract, full-text method passage, replicated experiment and independently evaluated measurement warrant different levels of inference. Store the exact evidence-access tier for each claim.
concepts.title: Claim-to-source support levels and public abstracts

concepts.applicability: Model and agent workflows combining cached reference summaries with question answering.
concepts.limitations: Matching a word in a concept title does not establish a source supporting the requested conclusion.
concepts.summary: A reusable reference must explicitly abstain or request additional investigation when topical lexical retrieval does not cover the question. A related reference cannot substantiate a causal, therapeutic, or universal claim outside its scope.
concepts.title: Research fallback when scoped references are insufficient

concepts.applicability: Repeated research tasks with known cost accounting and predeclared quality metrics.
concepts.limitations: The EPRA example is synthetic and no energy or GPU savings are demonstrated for this repository.
concepts.summary: A reusable evidence layer is useful when construction and maintenance costs are amortized across enough eligible queries without reducing answer quality, freshness or citation fidelity relative to appropriate baselines.
concepts.title: Measure amortization with answer-quality constraints

concepts.applicability: Parameter inference from plate or acoustic resonance patterns, with experimental boundary conditions noted.
concepts.limitations: An identifiability claim must be demonstrated for the chosen model and observation set; this record is a general caution.
concepts.summary: A modal frequency or nodal image need not uniquely determine support type or material parameters; distinct physical systems may exhibit overlapping spectra and similar mode shapes.
concepts.title: Non-unique inversion from resonance geometry

concepts.applicability: Reporting measured modal frequency, displacement, drive or sensor response.
concepts.limitations: These are metrological reporting principles, not a claim that the Atlas has calibrated any hardware.
concepts.summary: An experimental result should state uncertainty components and how they were estimated. If expanded uncertainty is reported, identify the coverage factor and basis for its interpretation.
concepts.title: Standard uncertainty and coverage factors

concepts.applicability: Importing experimental spectra, especially when comparing excitation and observed resonances.
concepts.limitations: Metadata supplied by an operator do not independently establish that the instrument was actually calibrated.
concepts.summary: A frequency-response observation must carry its collection method, instrument identity, calibration reference, units, sample uncertainty, apparatus and boundary conditions to remain interpretable across systems.
concepts.title: Instrument and calibration provenance

concepts.applicability: Machine-readable exports and research archive exchange across independent agents.
concepts.limitations: FAIR is a design guideline. Content rights, authentication and actual semantic compatibility still require checks.
concepts.summary: The FAIR principles call for persistent identifiers, rich metadata, interoperable representation, qualified links and reusable provenance. They guide the design of Atlas exports, not proof that every record is compliant.
concepts.title: Findable interoperable reusable scientific records

concepts.applicability: Maintaining the trust status and refresh policy of cited research sources.
concepts.limitations: An absent update flag in a local snapshot is not evidence that the article has never been updated or retracted.
concepts.summary: Scholarly records may be updated by separately identified corrections, concerns, withdrawals or retractions; a reader should follow authoritative notices and not assume a prior PDF is up-to-date.
concepts.title: Publisher corrections and retraction notices

concepts.applicability: Source-change monitoring and alert propagation in a reusable reference library.
concepts.limitations: Metadata checks can be incomplete; local operator-submitted notices are not independently authenticated.
concepts.summary: A report about a publication update is a lead for adjudication. Notice identity, target work, update type, publication date and scope must be checked before changing the scientific standing of dependent claims.
concepts.title: Update signals versus verified conclusions

concepts.applicability: History of experimental cymatics and interpretation of visually observed particle patterns.
concepts.limitations: The archival catalog verifies publication provenance, not a new experimental replication or a full reading of the manuscript.
concepts.summary: Faraday documented historical observations of fine particles forming distinct configurations on vibrating elastic surfaces. This is a primary historical account of particle motion and patterns, not a universal pattern-frequency formula.
concepts.title: Faraday 1831: observing particles on vibrating elastic surfaces

aliases: first order and second order acoustofluidics
concepts.applicability: Analytical treatment of ultrasound resonance and acoustically driven fluid motion in microchannels under small-perturbation assumptions.
concepts.limitations: This model is not interchangeable with elastic plate modes or free-surface parametric Faraday waves; material and thermal assumptions matter.
concepts.summary: Small-amplitude sound fields in fluids can be modeled through perturbation expansions of density, pressure and velocity, separating first-order oscillations from second-order time-averaged motion.
concepts.title: First- and second-order perturbation models in acoustofluidics

concepts.applicability: Comparisons and design calculations for microchannel particle motion under sound fields.
concepts.limitations: Source is a tutorial-level publisher abstract; specific formulas and device performance must be verified in the full paper and with actual device conditions.
concepts.summary: Acoustophoretic particle manipulation can be analyzed by scaling physical forces and characteristic lengths, times and amplitudes relevant to microfluidic systems.
concepts.title: Scaling laws for acoustophoretic device design

concepts.applicability: Planning reproducible plate experiments and comparing arrangements with different actuation and supports.
concepts.limitations: Specific thickness observations were reported for the original brass samples; they cannot be generalized to every plate and material.
concepts.summary: Experimental plates with different thickness, mounting, and vibration excitation can produce different or distorted nodal figures. Historical measurements by Colwell describe using speaker-driven excitation of thin brass plates.
concepts.title: Chladni plate patterns depend on excitation and mounting

aliases: measured height field Faraday waves dataset
concepts.applicability: External reproducibility research in wave-surface observations, imaging and inference.
concepts.limitations: Only Dryad public descriptive metadata was inspected; its 601 MB archive is not downloaded or analyzed by this Atlas. Dataset status is external and unvalidated here.
concepts.summary: Strickland and collaborators deposited experimental surface-height and fluorescent surfactant-density measurements for driven gravity-capillary waves, including standing Faraday and traveling meniscus components.
concepts.title: Published Faraday-wave surface-height and surfactant measurements

aliases: drum membrane measured modal frequencies dataset
Zenodo Wijnand tom tom Chladni videos
concepts.applicability: External empirical comparisons of membrane vibration, frequency shifts and feedback-control studies.
concepts.limitations: The Zenodo dataset is external; no video, audio or numeric measurement files were imported, checked or reproduced in this release.
concepts.summary: A 2026 Zenodo research deposit describes pressure, membrane-frequency and control measurements and supplementary Chladni-figure videos for an experimental tom-tom drum vibration system.
concepts.title: Published drum membrane mode-shift measurements and Chladni video

mission: Reusable, source-linked, uncertainty-aware scientific reference infrastructure for any authorized agent, model or software system.

policy.reference_status: curated editorial synopsis, not independent experimental validation
policy.source_status: Source records carry individual metadata_checked dates (2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11); source pages may change and publication statuses are not monitored live.
policy.update: Append new version, preserve the old exported manifest and investigate conflicts
policy.usage: Cite provided source URLs; honor conditions and limitations; do not silently upgrade to verified experiment
